description: A VP of Infrastructure must approve the autoscaling and operating policy for the checkout Kubernetes cluster before the next production traffic cycle, with input from reliability, finance, application operations, and security engineering.

shared_context.S1: The checkout Kubernetes cluster currently scales between 10 and 30 nodes, with automatic consolidation enabled.
shared_context.S2: The cluster has passed its routine availability tests, and the next production traffic cycle begins Monday morning.
shared_context.S3: Morgan has final approval authority for the cluster's autoscaling and operating policy.
shared_context.S4: The infrastructure operating review routinely asks reliability, finance, checkout operations, and security to report any constraints before Morgan approves a policy.

PF1.text: During an overnight load replay yesterday, Riley measured that checkout latency breaches its 300 ms target whenever this workload has fewer than 18 nodes; Riley has not filed the measurement because the replay was part of a separate reliability investigation.

PF2.text: While reconciling this month's cloud invoice thirty minutes ago, Casey confirmed that the approved cost model allows a maximum of 24 nodes but not 30 during a sustained burst; the finance correction is still waiting for its normal ticket.

PF3.text: During a shard-rebalancing rehearsal this morning, Taylor confirmed that automatic consolidation must be disabled from 02:00 to 04:00 UTC or checkout shard movement can interrupt active sessions; Taylor has not updated the operations runbook yet.

PF4.text: During a security baseline review today, Jordan confirmed that checkout pods may scale only onto the hardened node pool because the standard pool exposes a node-local metadata path; the finding is awaiting a formal security ticket.

acceptance_conditions: The autoscaling minimum must be exactly 18 nodes.
The autoscaling maximum must be exactly 24 nodes.
Automatic consolidation must be disabled from 02:00 to 04:00 UTC.
Checkout workloads must use the hardened node pool.
A reliability capacity commitment must be recorded.
A cloud-cost policy commitment must be recorded.
A shard-rebalance operating-window commitment must be recorded.
A hardened-node-pool security commitment must be recorded.
The latency measurement must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C5: any('18' in c['detail'] and 'latency' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any('24' in c['detail'] and 'cost' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('02:00' in c['detail'] and '04:00' in c['detail'] and ('consolidation' in c['detail'] or 'runbook' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('hardened' in c['detail'] and ('node pool' in c['detail'] or 'security' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The measured latency boundary changes the minimum from the current generic 10-node floor to exactly 18 nodes and creates a reliability capacity commitment.
The confirmed cost model changes the maximum from the current 30-node ceiling to exactly 24 nodes and creates the cloud-cost policy commitment.
The shard-rebalancing result changes consolidation from continuously enabled to disabled specifically during 02:00-04:00 UTC and creates the operating-window commitment.
The metadata-path finding changes the eligible checkout placement from the ordinary node pool to the hardened pool and creates the hardened-pool security commitment.
